summary: Targets the largest remaining full-layer gap (decode_1 27.2 us vs floor 4.3, FA3 main+combine+norm-gate ~22.8 us) with a kernel that stage 2 already proved correct for one request spanning every CTA. The design is sound and M2 (<=16 us) is plausible from the chunk320 evidence (A 11.0 + combine 4.5). The fixed choices, grid = SM count and two-level ticket, are untested and should be bracketed by in-process eager diagnostics, not by a separate okc run.
justification: Stage 2 (job e592b1f5d3db4f83, 1.4171 [1.396,1.443] vs best 1.3949 [1.374,1.416], unproven-vs-best only because the CIs overlap) made a real, attributable kernel gain: full decode_16 shape 122.8 -> 110.9 us (A+B 120.0 -> splitkv_attn_sk_kernel 108.9), full decode_32 241.9 -> 226.8 us (A+B 254.3 -> 226.8); every other shape within ~1 us of best. M1 met on both; M2 narrowly missed (108.9 vs <=108, 226.8 vs <=222). The in-process diagnostics split it: stream-K work split alone gave 1.10x/1.14x on kernel A (117.5 -> 106.9, 245.3 -> 215.1 us eager), while the ticket fold saved only 1.05x/1.03x net: the ticket kernel is ~5.8/6.2 us slower than the no-ticket kernel, i.e. the serialized last-arriver merge tail costs ~6 us against the 11.7 us separate combine it replaces. A: stage 2's in-kernel ticket path already passed the self-check for 'B=2 one request spans every CTA' at grids 7 and 264, so widening the gate to batch 1 reuses a correct kernel. Prior batch-1 evidence: full-decode1-cuda-splitkv-chunk320 ran stage-1 A in 11.0 us (20.5 MB, ~1.86 TB/s) + combine 4.5 + pre-attn 1.4 = 19.5 us shape, vs 27.3 on FA3. It lost only through its unrelated chunk change at decode_32, which this gate avoids (batch > 1 keeps the stage-2 code). Stream-K over 1250 64-token tiles removes chunk quantization, and folding combine + norm-gate removes ~8 us of launches and kernels. A realistic target is attention ~8-11 us (ramp-dominated at only ~9.5 tiles per CTA) + merge ~1-2 us + pre-attn 1.4, giving 11-14 us: M2 likely, M3 (<=12) possible. Expected directions are consistent: decode_1 full weight 16; decode_16/32 should be byte-identical to stage 2 (the same grid and single-level ticket at batch > 1); sliding and verify are gated out. Merge cost: with 132 partials of 16x64 fp32 (+m,l), single-level is ~0.55 MB read serially by one CTA after the last arrival. At B=16 (~17 slots per request) the stage-2 diagnostics already attribute ~6 us of tail to the ticket path, so a two-level merge at nseg 132 is the right design point. WEAKEST LINK: grid = SM count at batch 1. It halves the CTAs (and the bytes in flight) vs the 2-CTA/SM residency the kernel was tuned for (113 regs, 95 KB smem, 2 CTAs/SM), and each CTA's fixed prologue (prefix load, meta prefetch, ring fill, q fetch) dominates a ~9.5-tile range. Grid 264 halves the per-CTA work instead, which may hide the ramp better, at the cost of 264 partials (G=17). Nothing in the record says which wins; the hypothesis fixes one config with no measurement. A secondary weak point: the 2.7-2.9 TB/s bandwidth figure comes from 328-655 MB runs. A 20.5 MB kernel lasts ~7 us, so ramp-up and the tail matter, and the 7.5 us estimate is optimistic.
confounders: full-decode-splitkv-s2-streamk-ticket-inproc (parent, not on master): decode_16/32 should reproduce stage 2 exactly (110.9/226.8). The headline vs BEST mixes stage 2's own gain into this run, so judge decode_1 by top_kernels: the target is the v2 kernel plus pre-attn replacing FA3 main 14.7 + FlashAttnFwdCombine 7.0 + norm_gate 1.1.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: batch 1 already takes the unpaired q layout (paired requires batch > 1), and 'and not splitkv' keeps it unpaired once the gate widens. Consistent, no confound; but if the gate widening is written into _splitkv_gate, check that the pairing predicate and the q allocation still agree at batch 1.
fused-preattention-triton: the batch-1 pre-attn (1.4 us, unpaired) is kept as is; it neighbours the kernel only in launch order.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv (v1) and the earlier chunk320/chunk640 attempts: same-area prior results (neutral). They are the evidence base, not confounders, because v1 is not on the batch-1 path here.
interference: No okc companion is warranted. Both sub-decisions (grid SM vs 2xSM, single- vs two-level ticket) are config or template switches of one kernel, and they are best bracketed in-process on the same GPU, as stage 2 did with its diagnostics. Ask the builder to print eager cold-L2 timings at synthetic B=1 x 80000 for: (a) the stage-2 kernel as is at grid 2xSM (single-level, the widen-gate-only control), (b) grid SM single-level, (c) grid SM two-level (the timed path), (d) grid 2xSM two-level, alongside master FA3 main + combine + norm_gate at the same input. That makes a decode_1 gain or loss attributable to widening, grid or merge without spending a check. Also print the two-level path's kernel time at B=16 as a diagnostic only (it is not on the timed path), which answers whether the ~6 us stage-2 tail would shrink at batch > 1. Rank by prepare timings only (LESSONS: they undercount the judge by 20-25%).
rules_flags: No rule problem found: the gate widening and grid choice are config-only (batch, SM count), gticket is a module-level zero buffer allocated at import from no input, the workspace is sized from grid and batch (shapes), and there is no host sync in the timed path. Every key is attended (the stream-K ranges cover all 1250 tiles), and P stays f16 (not FP8), so the FP8-P Max_offset lesson does not apply.

Graph-replay hygiene: each group's gticket must be reset by that group's own last arriver (not only by the final merger), and ticket[b] by the final merger. Both must reset after their last read. The self-check's 'two consecutive replays' and the 'tickets after self-check: sum 0' check should cover gticket too (sum over 64*32).

Group indexing: 'grouped by c // G' must be relative to c_lo of request b (g = (c - c_lo) // G), so the group count and membership are computable by every CTA from TP and grid alone. That is equivalent at batch 1 (c_lo = 0) but not in general; assert g < 32.
open_questions: Grid SM vs 2xSM at batch 1: which wins once ramp is included? Make the diagnostic decide it (print all four variants), or make the grid a second import-time selection from the printed timing (LESSONS 2026-10-25: pick variants from the printed timing, or assert the static choice is the fastest).

Does a 256-thread parallel single-level merge (each thread owns 4 of 1024 outputs and streams 132 slots with independent loads) already reach ~1-2 us, which would make the second ticket level unnecessary complexity?
Will the fused pre-attn of the sibling stage 3 (full-decode-splitkv-s3-fused-preattn) be extended to batch 1 when the two stage-3 branches are merged? 1.4 us is ~10% of the target decode_1 shape.

Block-scheduler placement: with grid == SM count and 2 CTAs/SM residency, check that the CTAs actually spread 1 per SM (it is usually breadth-first, but not guaranteed); the eager diagnostic's grid-SM bandwidth will show it.
